limitations_and_boundaries: The study uses mouse ES cell aggregates and may not fully recapitulate in vivo optic cup development; the role of surface ectoderm and lens is bypassed in this system.
Long-term neural retina culture beyond day 35 leads to loss of tissue integrity; further optimization is needed for functional photoreceptor maturation.
The computer simulation is based on assumptions derived from experimental results and simplifies the three-dimensional geometry to an axisymmetric model.
The AFM measurements were performed at room temperature, which may differ from physiological conditions.
The ablation experiments may trigger secondary wound healing responses that complicate interpretation of mechanical properties.

research_questions.statement: How does the optic cup structure self-organize from mouse embryonic stem cell aggregates in three-dimensional culture?

provenance.text_excerpt: the formation of the optic cup in the ES cell culture occurred in the absence of a lens (no crystalline+ tissue; n = 50 aggregates) or surface ectodermal tissues ... indicating that the invagination was not caused by external structures but occurred in a self-directed fashion

claims.statement: Optic cup morphogenesis can occur autonomously in 3D ES cell culture without lens or surface ectoderm.

experiments_or_tasks: Mouse ES cells were cultured as floating aggregates under low growth-factor conditions (SFEBq) with modifications: addition of 2% matrigel on day 1, or purified laminin/entactin plus Nodal during days 1–7. Culture medium was G-MEM with 1.5% KSR, non-essential amino acids, pyruvate, and 2-mercaptoethanol. On day 7, aggregates were transferred to bacterial-grade dishes in DMEM/F12/N2 under 40% O2/5% CO2.

methods.name: SFEBq culture with matrigel
methods.protocol_description: ES cells dissociated to single cells, re-aggregated in 96-well low-cell-adhesion plates (3,000 cells/100 µl/well) in differentiation medium (G-MEM, 1.5% KSR, 0.1 mM non-essential amino acids, 1 mM pyruvate, 1 mM 2-mercaptoethanol). On day 1, growth-factor-reduced matrigel added to 2% (v/v). On day 7, aggregates transferred to bacterial-grade dishes in DMEM/F12/N2 under 40% O2/5% CO2.

methods.name: Vesicle excision and culture

claims.statement: The retinal epithelium sequentially acquires distinct mechanical and molecular properties in a domain-specific manner during optic cup morphogenesis.

experiments_or_tasks: ES-cell-derived retinal epithelium was analyzed at phases 1–4 for pMLC2 levels, tissue rigidity (AFM), cell ablation response, and marker expression (Chx10, Pax6, Rx). Inhibitors: Y-27632 (ROCK), blebbistatin (myosin II), cytochalasin D (actin). AFM cantilever with glass bead (100 µm diameter, spring constant ~0.1 N/m) used to measure Young's modulus on apical side. Multi-photon laser ablation (900 nm) performed on targeted cells; gap closure monitored. Mitotic inhibitor aphidicolin (5 µM) used to assess proliferation role in gap filling.

methods.name: AFM-based tissue rigidity measurement
methods.protocol_description: Force probe with glass bead (100 µm diameter) attached to tipless silicon cantilever (450 µm long, 50 µm wide, 2 µm thick; nominal spring constant ~0.02 N/m, with bead ~0.1 N/m). Measurement in contact mode using Nano-Wizard system with Cell-Hesion module. Tissues pressed with 20 nN force, approach/retraction speeds 10–20 µm/s. Young's modulus calculated from force-distance curve. Inhibitor treatments for 60 min at 37°C before measurement. All measurements at room temperature.

methods.name: Multi-photon laser ablation
methods.protocol_description: 900-nm laser beam from Mai-Tai Deep-See eHP at full power condensed on target cells via 25× water-immersion lens (N.A. 1.05) using spot illumination or line scan until cell rupture (0.4–2 s). Gap area quantified in optical sections over time.
